title.narrative: Multisectoral Returnees Reintegration Support in Homs and Rural Damascus

description.narrative: ltpgtLinked to envelope two of the allocation, NRC Syria proposes a 12-month integrated area-based project aimed at supporting returnee populations in Al Qusayr (Homs) and Babella-Hjerieh (Rural Damascus) to reintegrate into the communities by layering services on a community/neighborhood level. NRC’s needs-based intervention will focus on WASH, Shelter, and Education, complemented by NRC’s legal protection ongoing programme in the same communities. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe proposed intervention will reach 9,690 individuals, including returnees, IDPs, and host community members, in areas with a high rate of return and limited access to basic services. NRC’s integrated response builds on its field presence and assessments and will be self-implemented in coordination with other actors operating in the same areas—mainly the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), ADRA, and SSSD—to maximize impact, avoid overlapping, and promote effective community integration and delivery of coordinated response.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder Shelter, NRC will reach 151 returnee households (approximately 936 project participants) returning to moderately damaged homes through cash-for-shelter repair assistance. This approach gives households greater choice, promotes self-reliance, and contributes to strengthening the local economy by creating job opportunities.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtUnder WASH, NRC will improve access to essential water and sanitation services in both Babella - Hjeireh and Al-Qusayr. In Babella – Hjeireh, around 7,000 people will benefit from improved access to safe water through rehabilitation of a key water source and installation of a solar power system to ensure reliable and sustainable water access. This complements ADRA’s works in another part of the locality. In Al Qusayr, NRC will support around 2,690 people by rehabilitating damaged sections of the sanitation network, to prevent wastewater overflow, reduce health risks, and improve hygiene.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder Education, NRC will rehabilitate key learning spaces and deliver non-formal education (NFE) activities to help returnee children catch up on missed learning and reintegrate into the formal system. Support will also include learning materials and teacher capacity-building, promoting inclusive, quality education in line with sector priorities. These interventions are designed to serve both returnee and host children, reducing barriers to access and improve learning outcomes. A total of 700 children aged 7–14 in Al Qusayr and Hjeireh will be supported through non-formal education programs (remedial and bridging), with psychosocial support integrated throughout. 70 teachers will receive capacity-building training. Two schools—one in each location—will be rehabilitated, enhancing classrooms, WASH facilities, and reducing overcrowding. Parent-Teacher Associations and Children’s Councils will be established to strengthen community engagement and student participation. Additionally, 50 teacher kits will be distributed to improve lesson delivery.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe 9,690 individuals will be supported with documentation i.e., IDs and birth certificates, land tenure, and documentation and due diligence for properties. To ensure contributing to social cohesion, NRC will also target IDPs and host communities within the localities and will offer collaborative dispute resolutions through the legal programme. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtNRC will ensure meaningful community engagement through regular consultations and two-way communication mechanisms. The project will include sustainability measures such as training of community-based maintenance teams, formal handover of rehabilitated infrastructure to local authorities, and post-project technical follow-up. Monitoring and evaluation will be integrated throughout to track results, document learning, and guide timely and future adaptations.ltbrgtBy addressing immediate humanitarian needs while supporting longer-term recovery, this project contributes directly to improving the conditions of returnees and local integration, in line with SHF strategic objectives.ltbrgtlt/pgt
